overall: The AG found the Norfolk County Commission violated the Open Meeting Law by failing to timely approve its May 9, 2018 executive session minutes, but found no violation in the notice allegations and declined two others.

allegations.summary: A complainant alleged the commission improperly revised its October 3 meeting notice within the 48-hour window before the meeting to add minutes for review.
allegations.key_passage: Additionally, we find that the additional set of meeting minutes to be reviewed that was added to the notice on the day before the meeting was unexpected and therefore unanticipated by the chair at the time of the notice’s initial posting at least 48 hours before the meeting.

allegations.summary: A complainant alleged the executive session topic failed to describe the subject matters of the executive session minutes slated for review.
allegations.key_passage: there is no requirement that the public body describe the subject matters of those executive session minutes being reviewed

allegations.summary: A complainant alleged the notice should have indicated that there were two separate executive sessions held on July 18.
allegations.key_passage: nor indicate that there were two separate executive sessions for a particular meeting.

allegations.summary: A complainant alleged the commission failed to timely approve its May 9 executive session minutes, approving them only on October 3.
allegations.key_passage: Accordingly, we find that the Commission failed to timely approve the minutes because they had not been approved within the requisite timeframe of the 30 days after the meeting.

allegations.summary: A complainant alleged the commission did not certify when executive session minutes were written or identify the minutes-taker; the AG declined as not Open Meeting Law issues.
allegations.key_passage: Such allegations, even if true, do not allege violations of the Open Meeting Law and we therefore decline to review them.

allegations.summary: A complainant alleged unspecified violations at the October 3 meeting and asked the AG to independently audit executive session process and minutes.
allegations.key_passage: Our office does not conduct broad audits of public bodies based on generalized allegations.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the law's requirements
remedy_passage: We order immediate and future compliance with the law’s requirements and we caution that similar future violations could be considered evidence of intent to violate the law.
